ratings.note: 16px bold tag at ~3:1 is hard but not impossible to read for low-vision residents; the tag is extra information next to a readable time. (suggested 2)
The only route is a support call in office hours, so impact is 3. I put it one below the suggestion because the booking itself is kept and the phone route does work on weekdays. (suggested 4)
Every booking waits about 1.5 s with no change on screen; a second tap is then likely, which matters given the double-tap defect. (suggested 3)
Expiry is occasional; the screenshot shows Change slot right next to the dash, so recovery is findable even though the message does not explain. (suggested 2)
Van and trailer users with a missing or bad permit only learn about it at the last step, from an unlinked error; they can recover via Change vehicle. (suggested 3)
Every booking passes this step, but the cost is memory load and the confirm step restates the slot. Departure: I judge this minor. (suggested 3)
Residents who are doing something else often take over 5 minutes and lose the slot at the end with no warning; their details are kept. (suggested 3)
Blocks landline-only residents, often older ones; others get one surprise error. Departure: affects a minority of users, and a phone fallback exists. (suggested 4)

Every confirmation lacks the day, time and vehicle; there is a risk of arriving at the wrong time. Departure: the SMS reminder and the confirm step show the details, so I rate it major, not catastrophic. (suggested 4)
Same expiry state as the other finding; Change slot is visible and details are kept, so the cost is uncertainty. (suggested 2)
The screenshot shows Permit number on every car booking with no sign it is only for vans; car drivers hesitate and may go looking for a permit. (suggested 3)
About 1 s of blank slots on each day change; residents learn after the first time that slots appear. (suggested 2)
Only phones 360 px wide or smaller; about 32 px of overflow means some sideways scrolling or a clipped column. (suggested 2)
Everyone who changes slot or steps back lands on Today; the probe shows a Monday slot being booked without notice, though the confirm step does restate the day. (suggested 3)
Keyboard-only residents get no focus cue at all on the main choice in the flow. (suggested 3)
Overlaps the finding about reopening on Today; vehicle and waste are actually kept, so the harm is doubt and possible re-entry. (suggested 2)
Cancelled bookings (including those cancelled by a double tap) show the h1 Booked; the red status line is visible, but the heading and gate text contradict it. (suggested 3)
Only under forced colours; the selected day is restated in text below and exposed by aria-pressed. (suggested 1)
Today is the default day and same-day booking is common; the user only learns at the end that the slot was never bookable. (suggested 3)
Screen-reader users lose the progress cue; the page heading still names the step. (suggested 2)
A double tap silently cancels the booking while the page says Booked, so the resident is turned away at the gate with a loaded car. (suggested 4)
Every booking and every day change show nothing during the wait; this invites the repeat tap that cancels a booking. (suggested 3)
Same harm as the unannounced hold: residents who pause have no idea a hold is running. (suggested 3)
Same problem as the other done-page finding; I rate it the same. Departure: the reminder SMS mitigates it. (suggested 4)
Every day view; each tile shows its time, so misreading is a scan error rather than a likely wrong booking. (suggested 3)
Reading order and visual grouping disagree on every day that has Few left slots; the tiles still carry their times. (suggested 3)
The end time and the arrival rule are hidden on touch, but the intro states that slots last 20 minutes. (suggested 2)
Rare sequence; the inline error is clear. (suggested 1)
Only for a last-minute waste change; once you try Change vehicle, it is obvious that waste is on that page too. (suggested 1)
Design-token conformance; the user harm is captured by the contrast finding. (suggested 1)
Brief and resolves itself; the stale date label adds slight confusion. (suggested 2)
Departure: van permits are a core task, and older residents searching a council site with no link is a real detour that also hides the two-day lead time. (suggested 1)
Same-day bookings can take a slot that has already started; at best this is wasted steps, at worst a booking that cannot be used. (suggested 3)
